answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require time-locked collateral: each agent locks a deposit, like a walnut with a hard shell guarding value, before transacting. The deposit sits in escrow; honest agents reclaim it with yield, while agents caught running fake identities forfeit it entirely. Creating 1,000 Sybils demands 1,000 deposits, so attack cost scales linearly. A whisper network of peers flags suspicious clusters, and a bridge contract slashes deposits automatically when fraud is proven, no central arbiter needed.
